task.description: Security gate on Letflow.Entities.Record.Projector (replay_record/3, rebuild_projection/2) per docs/agents/instructions/security-invariants.md INV-1..INV-8, independently verified against the actual diff and code, not the handoff's own claims.

result.note: Scope test: this diff touches a tenant-data path (reads the event stream and rewrites entity_record_latest rows keyed by tenant schema prefix) -- SECURITY-REVIEWER applies. Per-invariant assessment: INV-1 (tenant data isolation) APPLIES, PASS -- verified by direct code read of lib/letflow/entities/record/projector.ex: both replay_record/3 and rebuild_projection/2 take `prefix` as a required String.t() argument, resolve it via TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 first (rejecting malformed schema names before any query), and every subsequent Repo call (EventStore.read/2, Repo.get(EntityTypeInstance,...), Repo.all(EntityTypeInstance), Repo.delete_all, Repo.insert!) passes `prefix: prefix` explicitly -- no caller-supplied tenant_id field is ever accepted or written (entity_record_latest carries no tenant_id column at all per its migration; isolation is 100% schema-prefix-based, consistent with 0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md). write_snapshots/3's delete_all is scoped `where: r.entity_type == ^entity_type` AND `prefix: prefix` together -- it can only ever touch the calling schema's own rows for the one entity_type being rebuilt, never a blanket delete, never another tenant's schema (Postgres schema-per-tenant makes cross-schema data structurally unreachable via a prefixed query). Confirmed (a) prefix-scoping present on every query, (b) rebuild_projection/2's resolve_entity_types(nil, prefix) enumerates only EntityTypeInstance rows in that same prefix -- no path to another tenant's entity types, (c) no caller-supplied tenant_id field exists on this table to disagree with the resolved prefix. INV-2/INV-3/INV-5 NOT-APPLICABLE (S4/S5 not started; no new API route or lookup-by-ID HTTP endpoint added -- confirmed via git diff --stat 9613d348, zero lib/letflow_web/** paths touched). INV-4 (secrets by reference) APPLIES (live), PASS -- grep for password/secret/token literals and System.get_env usage in the new file: zero hits; no secret material handled by this module. INV-6 (new data-access paths prove scoping) APPLIES, PASS -- satisfied by this handoff itself plus the INV-1 analysis above. INV-7 (no SQL string interpolation) APPLIES, PASS -- `grep -n "Repo.query" lib/letflow/entities/record/projector.ex` zero hits; every query is Ecto.Query/Repo.get/Repo.all/Repo.delete_all/Repo.insert! construct, fully parameterized by construction. INV-8 (no unhandled crashes on realistic failure paths) APPLIES, PASS -- `grep -n '^\\s*{:ok, .*} = ' lib/letflow/entities/record/projector.ex` zero hits; every fallible call (TenantProvisioning, EventStore.read, Repo.get returning nil, fold_record_events) is threaded through `with`/case tagged tuples; write_snapshots/3 runs inside Repo.transaction/1 so a Repo.insert! raise mid-loop rolls back that one entity type's writes cleanly rather than corrupting state (Ecto.Repo.Transaction semantics: any raise inside the fun aborts and rolls back the whole transaction). INV-9 NOT-APPLICABLE -- no outbound HTTP request in this module. Transaction-boundary review (item 2 of task): rebuild_each_entity_type/2 calls rebuild_one_entity_type/3 once per entity type via Enum.reduce_while, and each call opens its OWN Repo.transaction/1 inside write_snapshots/3 (one transaction per entity type, confirmed by reading the code -- the transaction boundary is entirely inside the per-type call, not shared across the reduce_while loop). On {:error, _} from one type, reduce_while halts the overall Enum.reduce_while but the PRIOR iterations' transactions already committed independently and are not rolled back -- this matches the moduledoc's own documented design ('so a corrupt stream for one entity type aborts only that type's rebuild; every other type's already-committed rebuild stays committed') and is the correct, intentional behavior, not a defect: partial multi-type rebuild leaves each already-rebuilt type fully consistent (delete+insert committed together per type), never half-rebuilt within a type. Own verification run (all real, not asserted): `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` -> clean. `mix test test/letflow/entities/record/projector_test.exs` -> 'Finished in 12.7 seconds ... Result: 10 passed', 0 failures. `mix test test/letflow/entities/` -> 'Finished in 42.3 seconds ... Result: 94 passed', 0 failures. `mix test test/letflow/event_store/` -> 'Finished in 50.9 seconds ... Result: 150 passed', 0 failures. No route/controller file added or changed (confirmed via git diff --stat). REQ-229's own implementation has no security defect on any applicable invariant -- PASS, routed to REVIEWER. Two items independently confirmed real but NOT REQ-229 defects, reported separately below and in the accompanying summary for ORCH: (1) Letflow.Entities.Definitions.get_definition_by_name/2 (lib/letflow/entities/definitions.ex lines 197-210) queries `where: e.name == ^name` with Repo.one/2 and no further filter, while entity_definitions' actual unique constraint (priv/repo/migrations/20260906000001_create_entity_definitions.exs, entity_definitions_tenant_name_shape_idx) is on (tenant_id, name, logical_shape_version) -- confirmed by direct read of both files. Two active-version rows sharing a name (a legitimate outcome of REQ-225/226's own versioning design, reached via create_definition/2 + activate_definition/4 called twice for the same name) makes Repo.one/2 raise Ecto.MultipleResultsError instead of returning a typed result, violating this same file's own INV-8 principle (unhandled crash on realistic, tenant-reachable input) on the ALREADY-SHIPPED REQ-226 code path -- and per this handoff's own task, delete_record/2 (which calls get_definition_by_name/2 via fetch_active_definition/2) inherits the crash. Assessed as availability/DoS-class, not a data-exposure or cross-tenant leak: the crash is a 500-class failure reachable by a tenant against their own entity type after their own legitimate multi-version workflow, not an attacker gaining access to another tenant's data or bypassing authorization. Recommend filing as a new issue against REQ-226 (get_definition_by_name/2 should select the latest/active row deterministically, e.g. order_by status/inserted_at + limit 1, or explicitly document and enforce single-active-version-per-name at the activation step) rather than blocking REQ-229, since REQ-229 did not introduce it and does not call this function itself. (2) Letflow.TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 (lib/letflow/tenant_provisioning.ex lines 194-209) confirmed by direct read: both clauses of the function -- the `with` chain's `else` branch and the fallback function head for non-binary input -- resolve to {:error, :invalid_schema_name} only; there is no code path anywhere in the function that produces {:error, :tenant_not_provisioned}. This is genuinely dead code carried into replay_error()/rebuild_error() type unions for design-doc parity, not a security defect (no invariant depends on this variant being reachable) -- lower priority than item 1, informational only, no action required beyond what ELIXIR-DEV already flagged in the moduledoc.
